title: Hightide Retail POC - traffic patterns, SLA & token mix scoping
summary: Discovery-style POC scoping between Redwood AE/SE and Hightide Retail. Main goal: define workload profile for a 4-week POC that proves p95 latency under 150ms at expected QPS and shows cost per 1M tokens. Discussed traffic shape (steady + flash sales spikes), token mix (short queries + long receipts), benchmark strategy (replay production traces), required telemetry and security constraints. Agreed next steps: Redwood to share benchmark plan, pricing model and run an initial test harness with sample traces; Hightide to share redacted production trace and approval for VPC networking for Private run.
next_steps: Maya: share POC benchmark plan and template spreadsheet by 2025-11-24
Samir: prepare a lightweight replay harness and sample k6 script by 2025-11-26
Laura: provide redacted request traces and token histograms by 2025-11-25
Rajiv: confirm networking constraints and whether Private deployment needed for the POC by 2025-11-27
Schedule follow-up demo/benchmarks review for week of 2025-12-01
action_items: Maya Chen: send latency/cost model spreadsheet (includes batching sims) - due 2025-11-24
Samir Patel: spin up replay harness in Redwood sandbox and share runbook - due 2025-11-26
Laura Kim: export 7 days of redacted trace, token counts, and percentiles - due 2025-11-25
Rajiv Menon: confirm whether Hightide requires Private/VPC for POC and provide KMS contact - due 2025-11-27
header:
Date: 2025-11-20 16:00 PST
Duration: 56m
Location: Zoom
Recording: enabled
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Laura Kim (Hightide Head of ML), Rajiv Menon (Infra), Ellen Price (Product)
transcript:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll kick off — quick intros. I'm Maya, AE for Redwood. Samir is our SE. Laura: hi i'm laura, we run models and infra for personalization. Rajiv: rajiv here, infra lead. Ellen: ellen product.
[00:28] Maya: goal for today is to scope the POC — specifically traffic, success criteria, and what we need to run benchmarks. rough timeline we usually do a 4 week cycle, does that align with you?
[00:41] Laura: yeah 4 weeks sounds good, we wanna validate cost and p95 latency under realistic loads. major event is holiday flash sales so we need to model spikes.
[00:55] Samir: can you quantify the spike? like baseline qps and peak?
[01:02] Laura: baseline is around 30 QPS for the personalization endpoint, typical concurrency ~50, but during flash promos we see short bursts up to ~300 QPS for 3-8 minutes. there's also a long tail — some sessions issue long receipts 300-800 tokens.
[01:22] Rajiv: concurrency is interesting because our frontend multiplexes. We also have a small percentage of long-running multi-turn chats that keep KV cache hot.
[01:35] Maya: ok that's helpful. for success criteria, what are your targets? p95 latency? throughput? cost?
[01:43] Ellen: p95 under 150ms for single-turn personalization responses is ideal, but we might relax to 200ms for long generations. cost per 1M tokens and predictable billing is important.
[01:56] Samir: noted. on model side are you planning to use an open model or a vendor hosted model?
[02:03] Laura: we'd prefer an open-ish model, we tested Llama2-chat style internally but we're open. security wise we need SOC2 and VPC for data flows during POC.
[02:15] Maya: Redwood can run hosted POC or Dedicated/Private. For initial baseline we usually run a hosted sandbox to collect telemetry then move to private for final benchmarks if you require VPC/KMS.
[02:29] Rajiv: Private is likely for the final run. For the baseline it's ok to use a host environment as long as data is redacted.
[02:37] Samir: technical items to capture: qps ramp profile, concurrency distribution, input token histogram (mean, median, p95, p99), output token distribution, percent of requests that are multi-turn, cache hit ratio on prefix reuse. Also runtime SLOs: p50/p95/p99 latency, cpu/gpu utilization, KV cache evictions.
[02:57] Laura: we can export token histograms. I'll include p50/p95/p99. Expect input token mean ~40, median ~32, p95 around 210. Output mean around 220, p95 ~620 for those long receipts.
[03:13] Samir: that's a wide distribution; it affects batching and memory. For example, with 220 output tokens average you need to consider throughput vs memory for continuous batching, and worst-case KV cache growth.
[03:26] Maya: question on concurrency: are your clients using synchronous blocking calls or async multiplexed?
[03:31] Rajiv: mix — mobile clients mostly blocking for personalization, server side streams async for the ingestion pipeline. We saw a 10x temp increase during last promo because of a new marketing bot.
[03:44] Ellen: that was painful — our current provider started dropping requests during the spike. We want the POC to prove Redwood can gracefully degrade and route to a smaller model if needed.
[03:55] Samir: we can show a policy: primary model for quality, fallback to quantized smaller model under high queue depth, plus region failover. We'll include switch timings.
[04:08] Maya: let's talk bench harness: we'll need a replay of production traces with timing preserved, token counts attached, and a scenario for flash events. Our standard is to run a 24-hour replay plus targeted spike runs (e.g., 5 min ramp to peak) to capture cold-start and steady-state.
[04:27] Rajiv: we can provide 7 days of traces anonymized, but we need to scrub PII.
[04:32] Laura: yes we'll redact. do you support injecting synthetic long-turn sessions? we have some multi-turn flows that rarely happen but are critical.
[04:40] Samir: yes, the harness can inject synthetic multi-turns. we'll parameterize turn length and KV reuse.
[04:46] Maya: timeline proposal: week1 onboarding + trace handoff, week2 baseline hosted run + quick tuning, week3 dedicated/private baseline and tuning, week4 final benchmark and cost analysis. Does that map to your internal timeline?
[04:58] Ellen: that works; we want a final run before holiday season so early December is good.
[05:03] Laura: on metrics we want token-level cost, per-route p95, and per-token latency breakdown. Also an audit log for requests for compliance.
[05:13] Maya: Redwood Console provides token-level breakdown and per-route dashboards. For compliance we'll share SOC2 and the audit logs sample.
[05:20] Rajiv: KMS integration — can you support our cloud KMS for key wrapping during Private runs?
[05:27] Samir: yes, we have KMS integrations and HSM options; we'll surface docs.
[05:32] Maya: any competitors in the running?
[05:35] Laura: we evaluated Anthropic and CloudProviderX managed endpoints. Anthropic had latency but cost was high; CloudProviderX is close but their batching transparency is limited.
[05:46] Samir: for the POC we'll show latency/cost tradeoffs and provide quantization/batching recs.
[05:52] Maya: a couple of clarifying items — what is your acceptance criteria for the POC?
[05:58] Ellen: three things: 1) p95 under 150ms on single-turn at expected baseline load, 2) no drop in request success rate during 5-10 min spike to peak QPS, 3) cost estimate within our target budget (TBD but we gave a ballpark in the RFP).
[06:14] Maya: we'll map those to tests. For the spike test we'll run repeated 5-min ramp scenarios with both hosted and private to compare.
[06:22] Laura: good. also we need to understand model versioning — can we pin model variants during the POC so results are reproducible?
[06:29] Samir: yes, you can pin a model version and we can snapshot the runtime config. We'll include a roll-back plan and explain kernel selection and quantization choices.
[06:38] Rajiv: logging — request/response traces should be available but redacted, with request IDs to correlate across our systems.
[06:46] Maya: that's standard, we'll provide sample logs.
[06:50] Ellen: what about failure modes — if a node OOMs during a spike, what's the graceful fallback?
[06:55] Samir: automatic fallback to a smaller quantized model variant and cross-region failover. For Dedicated we can reserve burst capacity to avoid OOMs. We'll show preset policies.
[07:05] Laura: ok. cost modeling — we need a spreadsheet that shows per-token cost under different batching and quantization setups.
[07:13] Maya: I'll send our cost model template. It will accept inputs: qps, avg tokens in/out, batching latency targets, and output estimated $/1M tokens.
[07:21] Rajiv: please include assumptions about GPU types and memory overhead.
[07:25] Samir: will do.
[07:28] Maya: any compliance paperwork you need ahead of Private run?
[07:31] Rajiv: we have a security review; SOC2 attestation and data flow diagrams would help. Also SAML/SSO for console access.
[07:40] Maya: we have SOC2 docs and SSO integration guides, will share links.
[07:44] Ellen: great. last thing — who owns success? who will sign off?
[07:49] Laura: i'll own ML metrics, Rajiv will own infra nonfunctional criteria, Ellen will own product acceptance.
[07:55] Maya: excellent. to recap next steps...
[08:00] Maya: action items — Maya share cost model and benchmark plan; Samir spin up harness; Laura provide traces; Rajiv confirm networking and KMS; schedule follow up.
[08:12] Ellen: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[08:15] Maya: thanks, we'll follow up with calendar invite and links to the shared spreadsheet.
[08:20] END OF TRANSCRIPT (truncated for storage)
